details: Bitcoin dipped below $63,000 as escalating military tensions between the United States and Iran, marked by fresh U.S. airstrikes on Iranian infrastructure and retaliatory threats, dampened global investor sentiment. The conflict, coupled with renewed U.S.-China political tensions following President Trump's declassification of intelligence reports, has led to a broader risk-off move across financial markets, with Asian equities also declining significantly. Rising oil prices due to potential disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz further fuel inflation concerns, negatively affecting risk assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: US-Iran Tensions, Trump's China Claims Push Bitcoin Below $63K

details: The U.S. Treasury Department and HM Treasury have revealed a joint framework for closer regulatory cooperation on digital assets. This blueprint aims to harmonize their approaches to stablecoins, tokenization, and digital financial infrastructure, fostering more seamless cross-border markets. The recommendations emphasize supporting a targeted review of international banking standards for crypto asset exposures and endorsing payment stablecoins fully backed by high-quality liquid assets, aligning with principles in the U.S. GENIUS Act.
title: US & UK Unveil Joint Plan for Cross-Border Stablecoin Regulation

details: Citadel Securities has made its first institutional investment in Crypto.com, injecting $400 million, which values the company at $20 billion. This strategic funding round is expected to accelerate Crypto.com's expansion across all asset classes, including tokenized securities and derivatives, aiming to create a more efficient 24/7 financial ecosystem. The move signifies a growing institutional interest in the convergence of traditional financial markets and digital asset infrastructure.
title: Citadel Securities Makes Strategic $400M Investment in Crypto.com
